claims.text: The trip record establishes the two endpoints and the booked optimal route: pickup at Jurong Point (1 Jurong West Central 2) and dropoff at Blk 311 Jurong East St 32, with optimal_distance_km 22.0 and optimal_duration_min 30.0. The rider's claim is measured against a real, recorded baseline, not an invented one.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02859, and the trace's first fix (2026-08-15T20:25:06+08:00) matches the trip_record's started_at exactly. The artifacts describe the same trip.

The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 92.0 km against a booked optimal of 22.0 km, an excess of 70.0 km. That is 318.18% of optimal, far past both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) and past both materiality tests (greater than 50% and greater than 8.0 km). The deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL on this trip's own trace.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 834 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. It does not meet any of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs, so no independent corroboration is required and the deviation stands on the trace alone.

The driver's only explanation is that the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination. That is not a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log: the chat log for this trip contains 0 messages, so there is no message from the rider, no timestamp before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and no waypoint_hint to corroborate. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and the excess is not reduced by it.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: the only advisory artifact is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the driver's implicit external-cause explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Under POL-RD-13(2) the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No amendment to the pickup or dropoff is recorded: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not re-baseline the optimal route. The 22.0 km booked optimal stands as the comparator.
The trip is not pooled: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline does not displace the 22.0 km optimal.

The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy. The fare_breakdown records charged_total 224.12, a surge_multiplier of 2.0 read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN (the trip_record carries no such field), and a recomputed_fare of 58.20 computed as ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 2.0) + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no airport surcharge and no promo discount. The refund is 224.12 - 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to 165.95 payable.

The refund is not de minimis: 165.92 is far above the SGD 0.50 floor. It is also not a full refund: 165.92 is 74.03% of charged_total, below the 90% full_refund_share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND rather than FULL_REFUND.

The rider has been charged and nothing has been returned: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0. A PARTIAL_REFUND therefore moves money back to the rider rather than leaving the present state standing.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due: the fare_breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and a zero tolls_erp line, and the airport_surcharge is 0.0 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no phantom line to refund under POL-RD-09(4), and no off-route ERP to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure under POL-RD-09(1).

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat-deviation pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 300, so neither the 3-or-more limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb of POL-RD-06 is met. The POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift is not available and the remedy stays at the POL-RD-02 partial. I note the driver's no_show_terminations_30d of 1 is a NO_SHOW_CHARGE field and is not a ground of decision in this category.

The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the 4-or-more claims condition is not met and no extra corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required. The rider's other profile fields are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground nothing.

The refund of 165.95 exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6), so the case must be ESCALATED to a human reviewer rather than finally ruled: no monetary outcome issues and the disputed amount is held rather than collected. I put this forward as the mandatory consequence of the arithmetic, not as a rider win on the merits.

claims.text: The trip record establishes the measured deviation on this trip: the platform's own routing engine put the optimal distance at 22.0 km, while the GPS trace records 92.0 km actually driven between the recorded pickup and dropoff events. That is an excess of 70.0 km, or 318.18% of optimal, which clears both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute) and also clears the materiality gate (greater than 50% of optimal and greater than 8.0 km absolute). The rider's claim of '92.0 km for a 22.0 km trip' is therefore arithmetically correct on the platform's own figures.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs and the trip-record figure may not be cited for the threshold test. Here the two agree at 92.0 km, so the threshold finding is safe on either reading, and the trace is the artifact that carries it.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 834 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, and no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required. The admissibility pre-pass agrees, tagging the artifact COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-02859 and the same pickup timestamp of 2026-08-15T20:25:06+08:00, and the excess of 70.0 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's counterparty statement - 'The rider was unresponsive and gave no destination' - does not discharge the shifted burden. It cites no evidence ID, and under POL-RD-08 a general assertion unsupported by a specific artifact and clause carries no weight and is discarded. It also does not engage any exculpatory clause: it is not a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04, not a road closure under POL-RD-03, and not a point relocation under POL-RD-05.

The chat log is empty: zero messages, no first or last message timestamp, and the trip record records a chat_message_count of 0. There is therefore no rider instruction in the chat_log that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04, and no waypoint_hint exists to run the 200 m corroboration test. The rider-requested-detour clause is unavailable on this record.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: the sole advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02859-01 is MISSING with a null payload and weight_multiplier 0.0, its issue detail stating that no advisory covers the Jurong Point corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's implicit traffic excuse cannot be tested against any advisory, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy rather than POL-RD-11. The recomputed fare on the optimal route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 2.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 58.20, against a charged_total of 224.12. The refund is therefore 224.12 - 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. 165.95. The surge multiplier of 2.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is the only artifact that carries it.

The refund does not reach the FULL_REFUND share: 165.92 is 74.03% of the charged_total of 224.12, below the 90% threshold in POL-RD-02, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND rather than a full one. The refund is also well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so no de minimis NO_ACTION applies.

The fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero tolls, so there is no off-route gantry charge to correct under POL-RD-09 and no pass-through amount to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The refund is confined to the distance-and-time overcharge, and the anti-double-count rule in POL-RD-09(1) is satisfied because there is nothing to double-count.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat-deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 0, against a threshold of 3 or more, and 0 divided by completed_trips_90d of 300 is 0.0, below the 0.05 ratio test. No POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral is available on this record, and I do not claim one. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names and is not relied on.

The rider's profile does not trigger the corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08: deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4 or more, so no additional corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required for this claim. The rider's other profile fields are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not relied on as a ground of decision.

The computed refund of 165.95 exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6), which is a mandatory escalation trigger. I note this against my own side's interest: on the arithmetic the case cannot be finally ruled by the automated pipeline and must go to a human reviewer with the disputed amount held rather than collected or refunded. I do not ask the tribunal to shrink the refund to avoid the trigger; the trigger is a function of the charged_total and the recomputed fare, both of which are fixed by the artifacts.

ruling.explanation:
This is a ROUTE_DEVIATION dispute filed by the rider over the Jurong Point to Blk 311 Jurong East St 32 trip of 15 Aug 2026. The deviation is established and material on this trip's own evidence, but the case must go to a human reviewer. Here is the reasoning for both parties.

DEVIATION. The governing distance is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02859), which records 92.0 km driven between the recorded pickup (20:25:06) and dropoff (22:43:56) against a booked optimal of 22.0 km (EV-TRIP-02859). Excess = 70.0 km, or 318.18% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and both materiality tests (over 50% and over 8.0 km). The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 834 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, zero gaps, so no independent corroboration is needed.

NO EXONERATION. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02859) is empty, so there is no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint; POL-RD-04 is unavailable. No pickup or dropoff was amended (POL-RD-05). The trip is RYDE_X, not pooled (POL-RD-12). The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not apply. The driver's counterparty statement ('the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination') is not a rider instruction, cites no artifact for any exculpatory clause, and so discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. The driver's profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 300 completed trips), so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral. No traffic advisory is on file (EV-ADVIS-02859-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0) and no party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 was never invoked.

REFUND ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02). Charged total (EV-FARE-02859): 224.12.
